title: Beyond Contextualisation: Developing an Integrated Curriculum Transformation Framework for Undergraduate Mathematics Through an African Open Distance e-Learning Case Study
content: Curriculum transformation has become a strategic priority across African higher education, yet limited guidance exists on how transformation can be operationalised within mathematically rigorous undergraduate curricula. Although scholarship has advanced important perspectives on Africanisation, decolonisation, curriculum coherence, mathematics education and Open Distance e-Learning (ODeL), these have rarely been integrated into a coherent curriculum-design framework. This study addresses that gap through a qualitative documentary case study of the comprehensive redevelopment of MAT1512, a first-year undergraduate calculus module at the University of South Africa. Documentary evidence comprising curriculum blueprints, study-unit drafts, editorial records, assessment redesign documents, multimedia integration plans and quality-assurance records was analysed using abductive thematic analysis. The analysis focused on the relationships among curriculum decisions and how these collectively enabled curriculum transformation. The findings indicate that transformation was achieved through an integrated curriculum architecture that coordinated contextual and epistemic responsiveness, conceptual progression, mathematical rigour, constructive alignment, assessment for learning, embedded learner support, multiple representations, purposeful multimedia integration and student agency. These principles were synthesised into the Integrated Curriculum Transformation Framework for Undergraduate Mathematics (ICTF–UM), which conceptualises curriculum architecture as the mechanism through which curriculum transformation becomes operational in mathematically intensive ODeL environments. The ICTF–UM provides a theoretically grounded and empirically derived framework for curriculum redevelopment, offering curriculum developers a transferable model for integrating disciplinary integrity, contextual relevance and learner-centred design within undergraduate mathematics in African higher education and comparable ODeL contexts.
